newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Eleven feared dead in Malaysia helicopter crash.
newsitem.headline: Eleven feared dead in Malaysia helicopter crash.

text.p: Eleven people were feared dead after two Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) helicopters crashed in a hilly area in eastern Sabah state, an RMAF spokesman said on Wednesday.

"Based on initial reports, there's no sign of survivors," said RMAF public relations officer Ramli Abdul Rahim. "The wreckages of both helicopters have been spotted but we're having difficulty reaching them."
He said the Defence Ministry was contacting the families of the personnel involved in the crash.
The RMAF said earlier on Wednesday that two Nuri helicopters went missing when returning from a routine mission in the remote district of Long Pasia in Sabah state.

The two helicopters were scheduled to arrive at their base on Labuan island off Borneo at 4.55 p.m. (0900 GMT) on Tuesday, it said, adding that the last radio contact with the aircraft was at 4.21 p.m.
The Defence Ministry did not say how the two helicopters crashed.

The latest incident brings to 14 the number of U.S.-made Nuri helicopters that have crashed since their purchase in 1968. Before Tuesday's incident, the previous crashes involving Nuri helicopters had claimed 60 lives.
In October last year, a Nuri helicopter crashed at sea while airlifting an injured Thai sailor to a hospital. Three crew members were killed in the incident.
All Nuri helicopters were grounded for nearly a month after the crash and were only allowed to resume flights after the air force was satisfied with their safety.
